content.text:
Operator
Good morning.
My name is Rob, and I'll be your conference operator today.
At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to the Herc Holdings Q4 and Full Year 2022 Earnings Conference Call.
All lines have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise. After the speaker's remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question during this time, simply press Star followed by the number one on your telephone keypad. If you would like to withdraw your question, again, press the Star one.
Thank you. Leslie Hunziker, Senior Vice President of IR Communications.
You may begin your conference.
Leslie Hunziker
SVP, Investor Relations and Communications, Herc Holdings Inc
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone.
Welcome to Herc Rentals Q4 2022 earnings conference call and webcast.
Earlier today, our press release, presentation slides, and Form 10-K were filed with the SEC and are all posted to the events page of our IR website at ir.hercrentals.com.
Today, we're reviewing our Q4 and full year 2022 results with comments on operations and our financials, including our view of the industry and our strategic outlook. The prepared remarks will be followed by an open Q&A.
Now let's move on to our safe harbor and GAAP reconciliation on slide three. Today's call will include forward-looking statements. These statements are based on the environment as we see it today and therefore involve risks and uncertainties.
I would caution you that our actual results could differ materially from the forward-looking statements made on this call.
You should also refer to the risk factor section of our annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2022. In addition to the financial results presented on a GAAP basis, we'll be discussing non-GAAP information that we believe is useful in evaluating the company's operating performance. Reconciliations for these non-GAAP measures to the closest GAAP equivalent can be found in the conference call materials.
A replay of this call can be accessed via dial-in or through a webcast on our website. Replay instructions were included in our earnings release this morning. We have not given permission for any other recording of this call and do not approve or sanction any transcribing of the call.
Finally, please mark your calendars to join our meetings and presentations at three conferences this quarter.
We'll be participating in the Barclays Industrial Conference in Miami on February 23, JP Morgan's High Yield Conference on March 6, also in Miami, and Bank of America's Industrial Conference in London on March 22.
With that, let me introduce you to our speakers.
This morning, I'm joined by Larry Silber, President and Chief Executive Officer, Aaron Birnbaum, Senior Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, and Mark Irion, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.
I'll now turn the call over to Larry.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
Thank you, Leslie, and good morning, everyone.
Let's start on slide number four. There's no question that 2022 was another exceptional year for Herc.
We delivered record-level financial performance across the board. Equipment rental revenue growth was 34% on top of 24% growth in 2021. In support of the rising demand, we invested $1 billion in net fleet purchases while improving fleet productivity, as evidenced by an annual increase in dollar utilization year over year.
We also invested in expanding our branch network by completing 18 strategic acquisitions and opening 21 greenfield locations in key markets in 2022. By focusing on rate growth and operating efficiencies, we've more than offset inflationary pressures as we delivered 160 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin improvement and 120 basis points of higher ROIC.
We're operating from a much stronger position today than at any time in our history with better systems and processes, more diverse end markets, a broader portfolio of products, a growing branch network, economies of scale, and a solid balance sheet. As one of the largest equipment rental providers with a national reach, our size, resources, and operational excellence are giving us a significant advantage in the marketplace. Moving on to Slide five.
From a macro standpoint, the North American equipment rental market generated 11% growth in 2022 on robust infrastructure, industrial, and other non-residential construction spending. Tailwinds came from a ramp-up in domestic manufacturing after years of inadequate investment, the beginnings of allocation of federal funding for construction projects, and the ongoing shift that is now taking place in specialty categories from equipment ownership to equipment rental.
Contractors understand better than ever the economic, environmental, and logistical benefits of renting equipment across categories. In 2022, Herc grew three times faster than the industry and gained a full point of share by leveraging our increased scale, network, and capabilities to ensure that we continue to meet the needs of existing and new customers and deliver on our commitments.
While demand has been strong, supply constraints are ongoing. We managed to secure the fleet necessary by leveraging our purchasing power, placing orders early in the buying cycle, utilizing our solid balance sheet, and capitalizing on our preferential position as a Tier One national equipment rental company.
On slide six, you can see the successful execution of our growth strategies also contributed to our outsized performance relative to the overall industry.
We increased revenue in our core categories of aerial, material handling, and earthmoving equipment last year by investing in fleet and optimizing our branch network. Revenue from our high-margin ProSolutions business also grew in 2022 compared with 2021, incrementally benefiting from new products, new locations, and cross-selling synergies.
Our innovative customer-facing digital capabilities were the catalyst to several new project wins late last year, especially at the national account level. You'll hear more about that from Aaron in a minute.
At the same time, we're committed to responsible ESG operating practices built on a strong cultural foundation, a safety-first protocol, and a pledge to continue to work hard to do more to protect the environment, often in partnership with our customers and suppliers.
Finally, between fleet investments, strategic M&A, dividend growth, and opportunistic share repurchases, I'm confident that Herc is allocating capital in the right areas and at the right time. We enter 2023 from a position of strength with a commitment to our growth plan, the strategies driving it, and the incredible people who execute it at such a high level.
On slide seven, in addition to continued strength in data centers, healthcare facilities, petrochem, and other key end markets, onshoring and fiscal stimulus trends have only accelerated despite concerns about a potential slowdown in the market.
These mega-projects represent the beginning of a multiyear flow of dollars into the industrial space. Every time you hear sustainability, climate change, and resiliency, you're hearing about growth opportunities for our company.
In 2021, we outlined our three-year strategic plan to grow and strengthen our core business, diversify our products and services, and operate more efficiently as we drive higher, more durable returns.
Today, we're tracking ahead of that plan as industry demand surpasses forecasts and we continue to follow the Herc playbook for superior performance.
With that, I'll turn it over to Aaron Birnbaum to take you through the Q4 details and provide some high-level operational drivers for the year. Mark Irion is going to walk you through the Q4 financial metrics and share our targets for 2023. Aaron?
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
Thanks, Larry, and good morning, everyone.
Our record Q4 results for revenue and profitability served as a great conclusion to a year marked by strong execution, geographic expansion, and new account wins. I'm really proud of the way our team continues to focus on delivering superior products and services for our customers while executing well against our strategic growth initiatives.
Execution starts with safety, and of course, safety is always at the core of everything we do. As you know from slide 9, our major internal safety program focuses on perfect days, that is, days with no OSHA-reportable incidents, no at-fault motor vehicle accidents, and no DOT violations.
We strive for 100% perfect days throughout the organization.
In the Q4, on our branch-by-branch measurement, all of our branch operations achieved at least 98% of days as perfect.
Equally notable, our TRIR improved to 0.52, a best-in-class result. On slide 10, our Q4 results reflect the market opportunity we seized by accelerating our investment in equipment with average OEC fleet up 31% over last year's comparable period. Equipment rental revenue also increased 31% compared with the prior year Q4. Our regional leaders and their teams are doing an excellent job placing our expanded fleet offering into new locations and with larger projects to incrementally drive the top line.
Our core business benefited from the continued strong demand for equipment all across all of our regions. Our ProSolutions business delivered double-digit growth year-over-year again in the Q4. As you know, ProSolutions includes our specialty categories of mobile power and distribution, climate control, remediation, and pump equipment.
This is a fast-growing, high-margin segment of the market.
We are capturing share here by capitalizing on cross-selling opportunities with new and existing core business customers, and leveraging the increasing density of our branch network for faster response. On slide eleven, you can see our fleet composition at OEC on the left side of the page. Total fleet is now a record $5.6 billion as of 31 December 2022, 29% higher than OEC fleet at the end of 2021.
You'll note that higher-margin specialty fleet represents about 24% of the total, and there's room to grow. Our fleet expenditures at OEC totaled $327 million in the recent Q4. At the end of 2022, we continued to accept new fleet deliveries despite seasonal demand slowdown as we prepare for additional growth in 2023.
We disposed of $140 million of fleet at OEC in the recent quarter, $80 million more than last year's similar period. We effectively balanced the need to refresh some older fleet while continuing to be prudent in managing our equipment level to meet strong customer demand and address the ongoing supply chain constraints. Proceeds from Q4 disposals were 44% of OEC and benefited from continued strong pricing of used equipment as evidenced by our 510 basis point margin improvement on these sales.
The average age of our disposals was 94 months in Q4, with average fleet age at about 48 months.
In addition to a best-in-class fleet, you can see on slide 12 that we have a diverse, well-balanced customer mix made up of large national accounts and local contractors across all business sectors in North America with a wide variety of equipment needs. National account business is benefiting from traditional end market demand and the increasing number of new multi-year reshoring and infrastructure projects being rolled out. In Q4, local accounts represented 57% of rental revenue.
Our goal is to have our annual split of local and national customer revenue be about 60/40 respectively. Our acquisition and greenfield strategy supports greater local account penetration. Slide 13 is a quick snapshot of the acquisitions we made in 2022. In Q4, we completed the purchase of two additional businesses with five locations, which brings last year's total of 18 companies in 29 locations as Larry mentioned.
As you know, we are focused on opportunities in high growth markets that complement our current branch network and fit our strategic, financial, and cultural filters. Moreover, many of the mega industrial projects being announced are in the geographies where we have focused our acquisitions and greenfield additions such as Texas, California, Ohio, and Arizona, and the cities of Phoenix, Houston, Toronto, Detroit, and Chicago.
We spent $515 million in net cash last year with an average multiple of approximately 5.5x. We see compelling revenue synergies in most every company we acquire. Over time, we can run the fleet and operations more efficiently, generating synergized multiples of approximately 3.5x to 4.5x.
Our acquisition process is now a core competency, having successfully integrated nearly 30 businesses with 62 locations into the Herc network over the last two years.
We have efficiently assimilated these companies, teams, equipment, operations, and customer accounts to rapidly add value to our operations in line with our urban market strategy. We have a very knowledgeable, experienced, and skilled team internally made up of region operators and M&A specialists who know our markets well and can leverage relationships.
This gives us confidence as we explore and evaluate new opportunities. As we look forward on slide 14, M&A is only one of our building blocks for future growth. Starting with our foundational core business, fleet CapEx and continued investments in greenfield locations provide the launching pad for incremental growth initiatives. Our ProSolutions business also has a lot of runway.
It saw growth through seven acquisitions last year in addition to a larger fleet, cross-selling benefits, and product line expansions. When it comes to winning new projects by raising the bar on customer experience, our investments in digital technology are making a difference. Our ProControl NextGen digital platform provides customers with more control and rich data to improve efficiency and lower costs on their job sites.
As Larry mentioned, we launched our advanced fleet management system last summer, and we'll continue rolling it out to our broad customer base this year. Another area of growth stems from our capabilities in providing customers with logistical expertise and full service on-site support.
As an experienced manager of on-site solutions, we are well-positioned to take the primary fleet management role on large projects, as well as to secure recurring revenue from long-term contracts for day-to-day rental fleet oversight, cost control, and maintenance at industrial customers' existing facilities. National accounts, as I mentioned, are also important to Herc growth as they are a legacy strength for us.
As large manufacturing and infrastructure projects continue to ramp up, we are leveraging a reputation and relationships to win more than our fair share of these projects from battery and EV plants to renewable and chip facilities. Among our 2022 national account customers, the average tenure with Herc was more than 28 years. We've earned their loyalty. National accounts, as you know, are characterized by high volume and longer duration with less seasonality and cycle risk.
Together, these initiatives represent the foundation and building blocks for substantial long-term growth opportunities for Herc, and our regional operations are primed and ready to advance our progress.
I'd like to thank Team Herc for their commitment to growth, operational excellence, and safety. Their professionalism shows up in the execution of our services to our customers every single day.
Now I'll pass the call on to Mark.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
Thanks, Aaron, and good morning, everyone.
The steady execution of our growth strategies that we just heard about from Larry and Aaron provided strength and momentum in our results throughout 2022 and into 2023. Slide 16 summarizes some of the excellent results we achieved in 2022. Q4 equipment rental revenue increased to a record $713 million from $542 million in Q4 2021.
A 31% increase, primarily due to continued volume and pricing momentum. As you heard, we're pushing hard on both our organic growth and acquisition strategies with great success. Taking a close look at the 31% rental revenue growth for Q4. About two-thirds of the growth was organic, and a third came from acquisitions.
This validates our ability to continue to grow our established core business organically, and our organic growth is approximately 2 times that of the overall rental market. Our smart acquisition strategy provides a nice growth supplement by allowing us to quickly bring on key rental talent, fleet, and customers to bolster our position in strategic markets.
Our ongoing focus on operating leverage continues to drive improved profitability and expanding margins. Adjusted net income in Q4 2022 increased 37% to $103 million, or $3.44 per diluted share, compared with adjusted net income of $75 million or $2.46 per diluted share in Q4 2021. Adjusted EBITDA increased 41% year over year to a record Q4 $361 million.
We expanded our adjusted EBITDA margin by 160 basis points to 46% in Q4 2022. All in all, an excellent quarter and an excellent year. You can see we made progress across every metric on this slide and are especially pleased with our margin expansion and RevPAR flow through of 54%.
Our business model drives fast growth and expanding margins, allowing us to continue to invest in our equipment, locations, and our people. In addition to creating value for our shareholders, which is clear by the 120 basis point improvement in ROIC in 2022 to 10.8%. On slide 17, the graph on the upper left illustrates our success in consistently driving rate growth.
This is always an important metric to manage, and it's especially important in the current environment with inflation creating cost pressure. In Q4, rate was up 6.6% year over year, with clear momentum as rate growth has increased in every quarter over the last two years. We will continue to focus on rate in 2023, and we'll push hard for mid-single-digit rate growth utilizing our proven and effective pricing tools, the discipline and professionalism of our sales team, and the rollover benefits from national account contract rate increases secured last year.
The backdrop for rate remains favorable as demand continues to outpace supply, and the industry appears to remain disciplined given the inflationary fleet environment. Our fleet size and OEC closed the quarter at about $5.6 billion.
The continued excellence of our purchasing team has contributed to the steady delivery of fleet in 2022, which was also supplemented by fleet integrated in conjunction with acquisition activity. Our average fleet on rent at OEC in Q4 is up 29% compared with average fleet growth of 31%. Dollar utilization dipped slightly in Q4 year-over-year to 43.5%, primarily due to a return to more normal seasonality.
That combined with our taking more fleet into the winter off-season than we normally would put pressure on utilization. In a normal supply environment, we place orders in Q4 and schedule deliveries for the spring in time for the construction season. In the current environment, we are placing orders almost a year out and taking receipt as soon as our vendors can deliver the equipment.
This will impact time utilization in the seasonal Q1 2023 as well. By taking the new fleet now, we ensure we'll be able to respond to our customers' demand this spring. For the year, we improved our utilization of 43.3% and continue to move closer to our target range of mid-40% based on our current fleet mix. For 2023, we're targeting incremental improvement in annual dollar utilization as we continue to focus on rate and as we return to normal seasonal demand patterns.
On slide 18, you can see we have no near-term debt maturities and have ample liquidity to fund our growth goals. Net capital expenditures exceeded cash flow from operations in 2022, with cash outflows of $250 million before acquisitions.
We'll continue to deploy capital to invest in our business and drive fleet growth in this strong multi-year demand environment. Our current leverage ratio of 2.4 times is well within our 2 to 3 times target range. In addition, we repurchased in excess of half a million shares of our common stock in Q4 at an average price of about $110 per share, and have announced a 10% increase in our quarterly dividend for 2023 to sixty-three and a quarter cents or $2.53 per share for the year. We remain confident in our business model and are committed to creating shareholder value.
The rental market chart on the upper left side of slide 19 shows the continued strength in our key end markets. The ARA estimate for 2022 North American rental industry revenue is $60 billion.
As Larry mentioned, that's 11% growth over 2021. There's another 5% growth forecasted for 2023. There remains strength in the outlook and the current growth cycle should remain intact. As we've discussed, Herc's rental revenue growth is eclipsing the broader industry growth rate by a factor of two to three times, whether you focus on 2022's total top line increase of 34% or our organic growth rate of over 20%.
We expect this outperformance to continue. In this environment, the advantages of scale are magnified and the big rental companies that have diversified end markets and the ability to service the current strength in industrial mega projects will continue to get bigger, faster. Two of our key end markets are industrial and non-residential construction, and both had robust growth in 2022 and are projecting solid outlooks for 2023.
Combined, these end markets reflect about two-thirds of our customer base, and both are likely to outperform other more consumer-driven end markets this year. Taking a look at the industrial spending forecast on the top right chart, IIR is projecting 13% growth in 2023 on top of 11% growth in 2022. Clearly, the industrial economy is strong and will continue to provide rental opportunities. These forecasts continue to move up for 2022 and 2023, which happened in Q3 as well.
When actual activity continues to exceed the forecasts each quarter, we are in a very robust environment. The non-residential construction starts also keep getting stronger, driven by an unprecedented amount of new mega projects that seem to be announced every day as the onshoring of US manufacturing capacity continues to gather steam.
Starts in 2022 are now estimated at $427 billion, for eye-popping growth of 42% year over year, the highest level ever. The chart in our Q3 presentation had growth projected at 19%. As I said, the forecasts are having trouble keeping up with actual activity. We should emphasize that these are also just starts of new projects and are being driven by multi-year construction builds that will continue into 2023 and 2024.
All these starts drive new non-residential construction put in place activity in the next year. Construction put in place activity is typically two times higher than the prior year starts. Additionally, there's another $293 billion in non-residential, non-buildings or infrastructure projects slated for 2023. That's a 17% increase over 2022.
There is growth all across the non-residential construction spectrum, and it is looking increasingly clear that our equipment will be in high demand in 2023. That is why we are leaning into the cycle and will be deploying capital to continue double-digit volume expansion to keep us cruising along in high gear. Therefore, as we move to slide 20, our guidance highlights our plans for outsized growth again in 2023.
Our planned net fleet CapEx of $1 to $1.2 billion allows us to maintain double-digit growth in fleet on rent. We should also see an increase in our used equipment sales in 2023 as we return to a more normal level of fleet replacement.
With the expectations for stronger operating leverage as we roll over some of the 2022 inflationary challenges, we estimate adjusted EBITDA will be in a range of $1.45 to 1.55 billion, representing another year of profitable growth ranging from 18% to 26%.
This guidance is organic, but when it comes to M&A opportunities, we have a robust pipeline that should enable us to invest another $500 million or so in acquisitions again this year, driving incremental growth to our guidance. Interest expense will continue to increase in 2023, reflecting the accumulation of the Fed rate increases and our continued M&A funding.
We are experiencing all of the trends consistent with an industry in an upcycle and intend to continue to drive excellent performance as our growth strategy remains in high gear.
With that, I'll turn the call back to Larry.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
Thanks, Mark. Everyone, please turn to slide 21. Everything we do starts with our vision, mission, and values, and a purpose statement that focuses on equipping our customers and communities to build a brighter future. We do what's right, and we're in this together. We take responsibility, we achieve results, and we prove ourselves every day.
Now, operator, please open the lines for questions.
Operator
At this time, I would like to remind everyone, in order to ask a question, press star then the number one on your telephone keypad.
Your first question comes from the line of Jerry Revich from Goldman Sachs. Your line is open.
Jerry Revich
Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Yes, hi. Good morning, everyone.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
Good morning, Jerry.
Jerry Revich
Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Hi. I'm wondering if you folks can expand, you know, on the M&A pipeline this year, Mark. Is there an opportunity for that to be over $500 million as we look at the impact of higher rates on a lot of the smaller players that are ABL funded?
To what extent could this be an outsized year of M&A relative to the $500 million target?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
I'm not sure. I mean, I think we're comfortable with the pipeline, and our goal is that sort of $500 million range. You know, if something opportunistic was to come up, you know, bigger than the kind of deals that we've been doing, we'd certainly look at that. That's the sort of level that we're comfortable with, and that's the level that we're sort of looking to achieve this year.
Jerry Revich
Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Okay. I'm wondering if you could just expand on the time utilization discussion. You know, you mentioned just the timing of gear deliveries means lower time utilization in Q1. Are you expecting an outsized pickup in time utilization versus normal seasonality in Q2 where we can return to time utilization we saw during the construction season in 2022? Or is that just running time too hot that's not optimal for the business?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
The construction season typically gets you into that sort of peak time utilization zone. So we'd expect to get back into sort of 2022 levels in Q2 and Q3. You know, it's Q4 and Q1 that we're highlighting with the sort of return to a more normal seasonal slowdown, plus just taking a lot more fleet than we typically would have had some impacts over the winter.
Jerry Revich
Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Got it. Lastly, you know, on the rate outlook, just considering the carryover effect to start the year, sounds like you're gonna be exiting with rate up in the, call it, maybe 3% range. Considering costs are slowing as well, are you expecting year-over-year margin expansion in H2 at that, you know, lower comp-driven rate number mark?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
I think you can see we've got a bit of traction in the flow-through in the H2 of 2022. We're continuing that momentum through into 2023, and we look to sort of see the, you know, range move from, you know, low 50s into that sort of mid-50 to 60 range. Typically picks up in the H2 of the year, similar to what you saw this year, just as you roll over the previous year's costs and headcount increases.
Jerry Revich
Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Super. Thank you.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
Thanks, Jerry Revich.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
Thanks, Jerry.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Rob Wertheimer from Melius Research. Your line is open.
Rob Wertheimer
Founding Partner, Melius Research
Good morning, everybody.
Hey. I had a question on acquisitions also, and you guys have obviously had a lot of margin increase over the last, well, two years, but, you know, including this year. I'm wondering if your targets are, you know, becoming, I don't know, cockier or having similar margin gain and less willing to sell. If you have any, you know, commentary on how the industry feels and whether people are still, you know, willing to come to the table with you. Well, look, yeah, I think, you know, the pipeline that we already have for 2023 is pretty robust.
We still see that there is ample opportunity, you know, for some further consolidation in the industry. We think, you know, we're in an excellent position to continue what we've been doing.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
We really don't see much of a change from last year or the year before.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
There's a big opportunity out there, Rob, in the smaller deals, which we kind of feel there's a bit more of an advantage for us. We're, you know, adding to a district where we need scale and being new to the M&A sort of game. We feel that we've got a, you know, sort of advantage on these smaller type deals, and that's where the volume of the opportunities are in the current market.
Rob Wertheimer
Founding Partner, Melius Research
Yeah, the multiples have been great on that. Just a small question, but I know you're trying to handle all the growth that's out there and all that you can, but if you had the opportunity, would you rather be doing a bit more replacement CapEx? Do you have a catch-up to do if growth ever slows, or do you feel kind of comfortable with where fleet age is despite the COVID, you know, back and forth? I'll stop there. Thanks.
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
We started to, Rob, in Q4, obviously selling more fleet for replacement CapEx. We believe as we go through 2023, as long as the supply chain cooperates, we'll get back to a more normal cadence. We feel good about where we are right now. You know, we're glad we started firing it back up in Q4 and feel good about the flow of new and replacement in 2023.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
That said, we're still concerned about supply constraints, you know, in the year. While we've managed to develop a fairly normal cadence, you know, there's still supply constraints from the OEM level that we're concerned about. Yeah. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from a line of Neil Tyler from Redburn. Your line is open.
Neil Tyler
Analyst, Redburn
Hey, good morning, everyone.
Thanks. Larry, your answer to the previous question actually sort of brings us neatly to the topic I wanted to ask about, which was in terms of that supply and the, you know, the gross CapEx number, I guess. You know, if we see a similar pattern to the demand side of things as we've seen over the last 12 months, namely that, you know, the initial forecasts end up being raised during the year and that translates into greater demand. Is there scope for you at this stage to add much more to your gross CapEx number, or do you see that demand manifesting either in terms of you matching it with accelerated M&A or through rate?
You know, you know, which order do you think those things are likely to stack up if in a better demand environment? Thank you.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
Yeah, look, great question, and, you know, a number of things to sort of unpack there, but, you know, we're pretty much, you know, have on order the fleet that we expect, and hope to be able to get in with a fairly normal cadence, over the course of the year. Remember, our fleet is fungible, right? So, certain markets might have some softness, and we'll be able to move fleet to those high demand areas where those projects materialize and where we can capitalize on that business. We still have some room in our CapEx, you know, if we choose to, you know, go after it.
The constraint there is the availability and ability to get it from the OEMs and their sort of limited capacity, as we go through the year.
Certainly, they've improved not to the level where, you know, we have assurances of what we're gonna get every month. We're still sort of, you know, we're still expecting, you know, certain amounts of material, there's still a fair amount of delays and rollover, you know, going on today. I think supply is more of the constraint rather than demand. Fortunately, as I said, our gear is fungible and we can move it.
Neil Tyler
Analyst, Redburn
Okay. Thank you. Is there any constraint on your side of things? I mean, landing, you know, $1.5 billion of fleet into your business is, you know, is obviously very different to the situation a year even a year ago or 2 years ago, certainly. How are the branches, you know, sort of able to cope with that and deploy it?
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
Neil, it's Aaron again. The branches are doing a great job absorbing the fleet. We've really spent a lot of time in the past 18 months developing our teams, expanding our teams. The network's bigger, through greenfields and acquisitions, and our sales force has been really developed very nicely to take that fleet, find new customers. Then over the top of that, you've got our national account team, which really has done a great job developing and nurturing the relationships we have on some of the larger projects in North America. We feel like all of our branches can continue to take fleets without any absorption issues in 2023.
Neil Tyler
Analyst, Redburn
Got it. Okay, thank you very much.
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
Thanks, Neil.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Kenneth Newman from KeyBanc Capital Markets. Your line is open.
Kenneth Newman
Equity Research Analyst, KeyBanc Capital Markets
Hey, good morning, guys.
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
Morning, Ken.
Neil Tyler
Analyst, Redburn
Hey, Ken.
Kenneth Newman
Equity Research Analyst, KeyBanc Capital Markets
Obviously, it sounds like demand visibility is very strong for 2023, driven by these large mega projects that we've all been talking about. I'm curious, Larry or Mark, is there any way that you can kinda help us quantify just how much of that visibility can be framed by the new guidance? You know, what's the guide kind of implying in terms of incremental infrastructure activity or opportunities versus reshoring activity?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
I mean, I think it's, you know, our visibility and our revenue mix is in that really specific. You know, we're just factoring in, you know, continued strong demand. These projects do take up, you know, big chunks of fleet when you get on them. There's, you know, a certain amount of visibility around that. Overall, you know, there's quite a bit of variability to the revenues and where they're coming from, and we're not specifically targeting, you know, growth in specific end markets. You know, you sort of look at that pie, there's growth all across those end markets. You know, we'll be targeting that, and we'll be looking to get our unfair share.
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
Yeah. You know, I think, Ken, you know, I look at the mega projects as sort of like the icing on the cake. You know, the overall general markets that we cover are all very strong, and the mega projects are just sort of additive to what we're doing. I don't view that as necessarily driving this improved demand. I think, you know, the base level of demand is very strong.
Kenneth Newman
Equity Research Analyst, KeyBanc Capital Markets
Right. I guess maybe to clarify then, I mean, just given how large these projects are, scale's a huge competitive advantage. Is it fair to assume that you're gonna punch well above your weight relative to your market share for these larger projects?
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
Yeah, I think that's accurate, Ken. You know, there's certain things that these large projects want, right? They want a lot of fleet. They want a high level of service, almost always an on-site type operation. They want technology solutions to manage the fleet and account management. There's really, you know, only so many national large players in the rental space that can provide all that. We do think we will, as others that are, you know, similar to us or big national players will be able to get outsized success on the big projects.
Kenneth Newman
Equity Research Analyst, KeyBanc Capital Markets
Yep. Just for my follow-up question here, you know, it seems like you are tracking much closer to that 5% market share target that you put out on your Analyst Day, I think back in 2021. You know, obviously the fleet still feels pretty tight from an industry perspective. Do you have any updated views on what you think market share gain capture could be relative to 2022? Or how do you think about longer term market share?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
Yeah, I mean, we're really happy to be moving that needle. Finally. That's been a long process for the company, and there's a lot of pride for us to be, you know, picking up another point in 2022. We'll continue along. We'll, you know, we're obviously committing fleet and capital to growing as fast as we can, and that should lead to market share gains, and we're happy, very happy about that.
Kenneth Newman
Equity Research Analyst, KeyBanc Capital Markets
Thanks.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Sherif El-Sabbahy from Bank of America. Your line is open.
Sherif El-Sabbahy
Research Analyst, Bank of America
Hi, good morning.
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
Good morning.
Neil Tyler
Analyst, Redburn
I just wanted to ask, you know, 2023 will be another year of large CapEx spend. Do you expect to be able to generate positive free cash flow? If not, what's the pathway to get there?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
Right. Yeah, no, we're looking at, you know, neutral free cash flow, I guess, at this level of fleet growth, with our current level of EBITDA expectations, before M&A. You know, while we're growing fleet at, you know, in the high 20s, that is a commitment of capital to growth, and that does put a challenge on free cash flow. The trade-off's really, you know, how fast do you wanna grow the fleet versus, you know, versus free cash flow. We're betting on fleet growth and market share growth, and we're doing that with, you know, improved margins, improved utilization, and creating shareholder value at this stage. That's the way we're executing on the strategy. It should be free cash flow neutral in 2023, before M&A.
Sherif El-Sabbahy
Research Analyst, Bank of America
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Steven Ramsey from Thompson Research Group. Your line is open.
Steven Ramsey
Deputy Director of Research, Thompson Research Group
Hey, good morning. Wanted to think about these mega projects some more. Are you able to cross-sell better just by the nature of these projects combined with your own internal improvements? Or do you have any initiatives there that maybe step up or what you're already doing?
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
These big mega projects, they pop up in different types of markets. Sometimes they're a little bit more rural than, you know, urban. With our footprint that we have nationally, we're able to support them. They typically always want a full suite of types of products. The core fleet, which we're investing heavily in, and then as they build those up, they do need a lot of climate and specialty solutions, because often they don't have shore power or permanent power inside the plant until it's, you know, further down the road of being developed.
They also depending on what their operation is and what they're doing inside the plant, they often need a lot of climate, heat or air conditioning dehumidification, until they get their permanent equipment installed.
It's a great project for the whole suite of services that we offer.
Steven Ramsey
Deputy Director of Research, Thompson Research Group
Great. Then do these mega projects support greater growth in your national accounts versus local? Then to capture more of this mega project opportunity, do you feel like you could invest more in branches, greenfield, or acquisitions closer to where these projects are happening?
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
The first question is, yes. Usually it's the big national type, mechanical, electrical general contractors that go in to do these projects. There's always an element of local contractors that are supporting the project as well. It's a great opportunity when you're on those projects to work with that all of that customer base. You often see the local customers get much larger and get more projects in the general area.
As far as us, I believe your second part of your question, Steve, was are we focused on new locations in some of these metropolitan area where these big projects are? I would say the answer to that is definitely yes. You know, we invested.
We did a lot of greenfield, a lot of acquisition activity in Texas, where we see a lot of this activity going on for one. We continue to strategically look at those opportunities for our footprint as it maps out with, you know, reshoring or big projects coming online.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
Yeah. Steve, you know, if a project's out in a rural market, we wouldn't necessarily look to open a branch or do an acquisition in a rural market. What we would do is an on-site, which would be for the duration of the project during its construction phase and operate from that type of a perspective. You know, we're not gonna chase, you know, flagpoles and chase customers to open, you know, facilities that would be permanent overhead. We would look to have temporary overhead in those locations.
Steven Ramsey
Deputy Director of Research, Thompson Research Group
Makes sense. Thanks, guys.
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from a line of Seth Weber from Wells Fargo. Your line is open.
Larry Stavitski
Equity Research Analyst, Wells Fargo
Hi, guys. This is Larry Stavitski on for Seth this morning. Thanks for taking my question. Just wanted to ask about quarter over quarter, any evidence of cancellations or push outs related to rising interest rates or macro concerns? You guys talked a lot about, you know, increased activity from infrastructure, construction, and some of these mega projects.
Just wondering if any evidence of project cancellations that you've been seeing.
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
Larry, this is Aaron. By nature of my job, I'm out in the field, at least half the month, every single month, visiting the branches, customers, and our sales team. You know, my ears are open to see if I hear any anecdotal concerns along those lines. I have yet to hear that. Every market I go to in North America, very robust activity, no cancellations, no postponements, no cancellation due to interest rates.
Most of these jobs are big, big planned investment jobs, you know, strategic reshoring, some public funding, and these projects are plowing through as scheduled.
Larry Stavitski
Equity Research Analyst, Wells Fargo
Okay. Thank you. I'll leave it there. Thanks, guys.
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings Inc
Thank you.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from a line of Mig Dobre from Baird. Your line is open.
Mig Dobre
Senior Research Analyst, Baird
Good morning. Thanks for taking the question.
I want to follow up on that last comment about really not seeing any cancellation and momentum remains strong. What do you make of the ABI index being below 50? I mean, obviously you have that as a key indicator for your business. I recognize that the mega projects are there, but what about the sort of regular mom and pop, for lack of a better term, of construction business?
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
Yeah. I mean, you can see on the chart that it's, you know, it's been, you know, below 50 since October. I mean, it's obviously coming off extraordinarily high readings before that. You know, it's maybe an indication of activity 12 months to 18 months out. You know, we're focused on the activity that's in front of us. You know, there's strong demand now. There's gonna be strong demand in the next couple of quarters, and that's what we're focusing on. You know, we'll adjust as necessary.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
To what the ABI might or might not be telling us, you know, for 2024.
Mig Dobre
Senior Research Analyst, Baird
Understood. A clarification, I don't know if I missed this. How are you thinking about gross CapEx? Maybe you can help us understand in your current outlook what the planned fleet disposals might look like in 2023?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
Right. Yeah, we're definitely gonna return to a normalized level of fleet disposals. That'll sort of pick up, you know, into that 2019-ish sorta range. You know, we've been running maybe in the $200 to 300 million zone of OEC for the last couple of years, and that'll sort of pick up to the, you know, $500 to 600 million zone, we expect. You know, the CapEx, the growth CapEx is rolling in faster than it was at the beginning of the year. We expect to sort of see improvements throughout this year. But we're getting a steady supply.
It's not as predictable as it is in a normal environment, but the supply is coming in, and we expect to be able to get enough fleet to execute on the plan.
Mig Dobre
Senior Research Analyst, Baird
Understood. Then maybe the last question, this is kinda going back to the answer that you provided to my first question that, you know, I understand that you guys are focused on the opportunity at hand here. But if conditions do change, right? If the ABI is actually telling us something valuable here, what are the things that you're looking for in your day-to-day business to make adjustments to either your CapEx or your cost structure as 2023 progresses?
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
Yeah, look, I think we monitor on a daily basis, you know, our dollar utilization, you know, across our districts and regions. We monitor our time utilization by category.
We look at what the seasonality is to make sure that, you know, the planned seasonality movement is happening as we expect, whether it's going into the spring construction season, we'll monitor that closely. Then as we proceed into the, you know, the hot weather to make sure, you know, we're seeing that seasonality adjustments happen with our, you know, our specialty businesses. Then rolling into the fall and winter, we have an adjustment there again in terms of seasonality.
We monitor that, and we monitor, you know, the things I just mentioned on a daily basis, not only at, you know, at our level here, but our region executives also monitor that closely down to our branches and districts. You know, we're very close to what's happening in activity on a daily basis, Nick. We make adjustments accordingly.
Mig Dobre
Senior Research Analyst, Baird
No, very helpful. Thank you so much.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
Thanks, Nick.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Brian Sponheimer from GAMCO. Your line is open.
Brian Sponheimer
Portfolio Manager, GAMCO
Hey, good morning, everyone.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings Inc
Good morning.
Brian Sponheimer
Portfolio Manager, GAMCO
Just very curious about the entertainment business. You know, you've touched on pretty much everything I wanted to talk about, but this was an exciting vertical for you. I think it's gotten a little bit softer. Anything you can add there as far as whether organic or inorganic growth is something you might be looking at?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
Yeah. I mean, it's obviously an important piece of the business for us. It's sort of been through some real cycles in the last couple of years. Real big driver of growth and mix in 2021 and less of a contributor in 2022, just as some of that, the growth rate slowed down. But you know, we'll remain committed, and you know, we're excited to the various parts of that business, both the sorta studio space and the entertainment space. It's an important part of our mix that we'll remain focused on.
Brian Sponheimer
Portfolio Manager, GAMCO
All right. If we were to think about your current level of revenue and what maybe a normalized CapEx steady-state growth would look like for the business at this size, what do you think that would be? Or, what do you think that would be?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
Well, I mean, I think we're certainly looking to catch up in terms of market share and grow faster than the overall markets. It's an opportunity for us, you know, as a strategy that we outlined in 2021 just to get in front of the cycle and really take advantage of the early growth opportunities. That's worked out, you know, even better than we could have imagined.
Growing at 30%, you know, is not sustainable over the whole, you know, life cycle of this company. If it was to sort of slow down to maybe 10% to 15%, at the end of the cycle, that would probably be a more normalized level, and that would create, you know, a lot more free cash flow than what we're currently throwing off.
Brian Sponheimer
Portfolio Manager, GAMCO
All right. Terrific. Well, congratulations on another great year. Look forward to seeing what 2023 holds.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings Inc
Thanks. Thanks, Brian.
Operator
There are no further questions at this time. Ms. Leslie Hunziker, I turn the call back over to you for some final closing comments.
Leslie Hunziker
SVP, Investor Relations and Communications, Herc Holdings Inc
Great. Thank you everyone for joining us on the call today.
We look forward to updating you on our progress in the quarters to come. Of course, if you have any further questions, please don't hesitate to reach out to us.
Have a great day.
Operator
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

content.text:
Operator
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Herc Holdings Q1 2022 Conference Call. All participants will be in a listen only mode. Should you need assistance, please signal a conference specialist by pressing the star key followed by zero. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star and then one. To withdraw yourself from the question queue, you may press star and two. Please also note today's event is being recorded. At this time, I'd like to turn the conference call over to Elizabeth Higashi, Vice President of Investor Relations and Sustainability. Ma'am, please go ahead.
Elizabeth Higashi
VP of Investor Relations and Sustainability, Herc Holdings
Thank you, Jamie, and thank you all for joining us this morning. Earlier today, our press release presentation slides and 10-Q were filed with the SEC and are all posted on the events page of our IR website at ir.hercrentals.com. This morning, I'm joined by Larry Silber, President and Chief Executive Officer, Aaron Birnbaum, Senior Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, and Mark Irion, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. We'll review our Q1 results with comments on operations and our financials, including our view of the industry and our strategic outlook. The prepared remarks will be followed by an open Q&A. Before we begin our formal remarks, I'd like to remind you to review our safe harbor statement on slide three. Today's call will include forward-looking statements.
These statements are based on the environment as we see it today and therefore involve risks and uncertainties. I would caution you that our actual results could differ materially from the forward-looking statements made on this call. You should also refer to the risk factors section of our annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2021. In addition to the financial results presented on a GAAP basis, we will be discussing non-GAAP information that we believe is useful in evaluating the company's operating performance. Reconciliations for these non-GAAP measures to the closest GAAP equivalent can be found in the conference call materials. Finally, a replay of this call can be accessed via dial-in or through a webcast on our website. Replay instructions are included in our earnings release this morning.
We have not given permission for any other recording of this call and do not approve or sanction any transcribing of the call. Now to turn the call over to Larry.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings
Thank you, Elizabeth, and good morning, everyone. Please turn to slide number four. I'm pleased to report that we achieved new records in Q1 2022 in total revenues, rental revenue, net income, dollar utilization, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EBITDA margin. Volume and rates contributed to the 32% increase in rental revenue over the prior year. Dollar utilization increased 280 basis points to 41.4%. Okay. Maybe that answers. Maybe I didn't ask it cleanly, but wage inflation and all the other pure inflation is maybe less than the, you know, 4% rental rate running right now?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
No. Wages overall are running mid-single digits, and maintenance expenses are mostly volume. You know, you sort of they are the big sort of drivers of DOE. Wages, mid-single digit is the biggest line item in there. Delivery and fuel is the next. That's got sort of 50% volume, 50% unit costs, and maintenance expenses are mostly volume.
Rob Wertheimer
Founding Partner and Director of Research, Melius Research
Okay, perfect. Two more. One minor one. When you do—I guess it's a fuel surcharge or whatever, does that come through as rental rate or is it separate? And then just if you have any comment on what pricing looks like from the regionals in the industry, whether the industry is kinda, you know, all following price increases. I'll stop there. Thank you.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
So fuel surcharges don't come through in rental rate. They do come through in the rental revenues if you look at the P&L, but is not factored into our rate growth. Yeah, it looks like there's pricing discipline across the board. There's a overall lift across the country, across the board in terms of size. Everybody seems to be focused on pricing.
Rob Wertheimer
Founding Partner and Director of Research, Melius Research
Perfect. Thank you.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
Sure.
Operator
Our next question comes from Steven Ramsey from Thompson Research. Please go ahead with your question.
Steven Ramsey
Senior Equity Analyst, Thompson Research
Hey, good morning. Wanted to dig in on raising the low end of CapEx. Just wanted to make sure, is that Q1 delivery being better or is that better delivery times in Q2 and Q3?
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings
Well, Q1 deliveries in Q1 were, you know, within expectations, maybe even a little bit better than what we expected. You know, that said, as Aaron mentioned just a few minutes ago, we continue to see some delays, you know, like 30 or 60-day delays. Now, you know, we've been experiencing that since the back end of 2020 and into 2021, so it's becoming more of a normal flow, even though the delivery days are being extended a little bit. We're just carrying over the past and we're getting the volume that we expected in the quarter. The volume of deliveries is, you know, on target, maybe a little better. We expect that as we roll through the year, it will improve and we should see obviously higher deliveries in Q2 and Q3.
Steven Ramsey
Senior Equity Analyst, Thompson Research
Okay, helpful. Then within the fleet, specialty equipment is nearing the low end of kinda that target range, 25% to 30% of OEC, currently. Do you expect to break into that optimal range in FY 2022, or is that beyond?
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings
I think over the next 12 to 18 months, we'll break into the median part of that optimal range. We continue to invest heavily in it and perform very well.
Steven Ramsey
Senior Equity Analyst, Thompson Research
Okay, helpful. Last thing for me, contractors are pressured obviously with the lack of labor and materials challenges in getting their projects done. Is this changing how long your fleet is staying on a job site and therefore helping utilization? Or is there some visibility into that dynamic potentially playing out into the busy season?
Aaron Birnbaum
SVP and COO, Herc Holdings
I mean, it's hard to tell. There's big projects out there. They're able to find their labor to get those jobs started. I think, you know, there's some sectors, maybe, oil and gas, if it fires back up, it's gonna be hard for them to get that labor to kinda get the rigs going again. That might be a problem there if they, you know, try to expand that vertical of business. We really haven't noticed it. Business is active and projects that are coming online, they're coming online.
Steven Ramsey
Senior Equity Analyst, Thompson Research
Helpful. Thank you.
Operator
Our next question comes from Ken Newman from KeyBanc. Please go ahead with your question.
Ken Newman
VP and Equity Research Analyst, KeyBanc
Hey, good morning, guys. Thanks for taking the question.
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings
Hey, Ken.
Ken Newman
VP and Equity Research Analyst, KeyBanc
Just wanted to put a finer point on the SG&A leverage into Q2 and the rest of the year. You know, I understand you expect it to improve versus Q1, but I'm curious if you think that the SG&A leverage could return to prior year levels barring another spike in fuel costs.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
There's not a lot of fuel in SG&A. That's not really a driver there. I think you'll see the same cadence. Well, you will see the same cadence going through the quarters where SG&A, as a percentage of rental revenues, is the highest in Q1 as it is in any quarter of the year. It will reduce as a percentage of rental rates going through the year, just with, you know, as the revenues increase and you get more leverage off of that. You know, in terms of flow through, we're sort of taking down our expectation or being conservative on our expectation with flow through. Most of that's in DOE, though. That's not really a SG&A driver.
I think, to answer that succinctly, we will get more leverage on SG&A, going through the year in 2022.
Ken Newman
VP and Equity Research Analyst, KeyBanc
Understood. For my follow-up, you know, you've spoken pretty positively obviously about the rate environment, about improving volumes going through the year. Can you help us kinda think about how you're thinking about dollar utilization? It sounds like, you know, you expect Q1 to be the low watermark for the year. Is it reasonable to think that dollar utilization is up year-over-year, every quarter for the rest of the remaining three quarters?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
Yes. Yeah, no, I mean, if you think about cost inflation going in, it impacts one year of your fleet. You know, we're holding that fleet for seven years. We've really got seven years to recover any increase of cost of the fleet with rate. That's not a real challenge, and that's really kind of a key thing to focus on in terms of having an inflation-resistant model. I think that's the way to approach it. There's sort of seven years to get back this quarter's cost inflation in the fleet, and we've got a very good shot at doing that.
Ken Newman
VP and Equity Research Analyst, KeyBanc
Understood. Thanks.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
You got it.
Operator
Our next question comes from Mig Dobre from Baird. Please go ahead with your question.
Mig Dobre
Senior Research Analyst and Associate Director of Research, Baird
Thank you. Good morning, everyone. I figure I'd just start with a quick clarification on your earlier comments, Mark, when you were talking about rental rates improving sequentially. Just to make sure we're clear, are you meaning that the year-over-year growth in rental rates will continue to accelerate sequentially as the year progresses? Is that how we're to interpret that?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
Yeah. I think we are looking to print increasing year-over-year growth from, you know, increasing from the 4.3% that we've got in Q1 each quarter going forward through 2022. That implies sequential rate increases.
Mig Dobre
Senior Research Analyst and Associate Director of Research, Baird
Okay. I see. Again, you know, given the base effects that you commented on, I'm sort of curious as to what gives you the comfort or the confidence that these trends can be sustained on more difficult comps as the year progresses. You know, maybe to an earlier question, you know, is it fair to assume that the exit rate on rental rates then into 2023 could be somewhere north of 5%?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
You know, when you just look at our history, we haven't had any commentary around base effects with rates, right? We've got an ability to raise rates each quarter, sort of year-over-year in this type of environment, and we're looking forward to doing so in a more favorable environment than what we've done it in historically. You know, if we're at 4.3%, we're saying it's going up each quarter, then it's heading up towards five. I think we're looking at certainly something higher than 4.3% by the end of the year, and we'll continue sort of pushing it, as far as we reasonably can.
There's not really a desire to run that up into a seven or an eight or go sort of and just put it all out there in one quarter. We'd rather have a steady improvement. You know, some of this is coming from our national accounts, where we need to sort of work in a competitive environment and just manage this in a modest way and manage the relationship with our customers. We're not looking to, you know, take advantage and gouge rates. You know, we need to recover the costs in our business, and we'll look to do that sort of steadily and modestly through the course of the year.
Mig Dobre
Senior Research Analyst and Associate Director of Research, Baird
No, sounds very fair. Thanks for that clarification. You know, a question on the flow-through on EBITDA. You know, you're pretty clear as to your full year expectations. You know, obviously we started pretty slow at 37 and change. I'm kinda curious as to how we should be thinking about the cadence of this flow-through. You know, do you fully catch up to that 50+ range in Q2, or is this more of a back half-loaded type of situation?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
Yeah. I think, I mean, you're right, it's H2 loaded. So there's a leverage. A portion of it's just lumps that we've got in Q1 that we don't see recurring in Q2. But a portion of it is just leveraging this investment in fixed costs that we've made with higher revenues as we build through. So as you get into your higher revenue quarters, which are Q3 and Q4, you get more leverage on that and improve the flow through. You know, obviously to get to 50%, you know, 50% to 60% for the year, it'll have to be higher than 50% in H2 to make up for the, you know, the 38% print in Q1.
Mig Dobre
Senior Research Analyst and Associate Director of Research, Baird
Okay. Sequentially, we shouldn't be thinking considerable improvement just given everything that's happening with costs. It's more of a Q3 and then Q4 event. That's what you're saying?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
Yeah. There's a steady improvement each quarter through the year.
Mig Dobre
Senior Research Analyst and Associate Director of Research, Baird
Then lastly, sort of a longer term question. You know, you provided CapEx targets at your Analyst Day. If my memory serves, it's $2.5 to 3 billion over the 2021, 2024 timeframe. You know, a few months have gone by here, and obviously the demand environment is pretty good. We have more clarity on infrastructure. I guess I'm kinda curious if your thinking on this CapEx through this intermediate term has changed at all in terms of either the low end or the high end. Also if the cadence in terms of how you're looking at deploying this capital through the period might have shifted at all. Thank you.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
That guidance was pretty much organic guidance, right? As the M&A stacks up, that M&A, those branches and those acquisitions, you know, take a little bit more capital, so that increases that number. You know, we're in line with our 2022 expectations, but, you know, probably getting more bullish into 2023. I think, to the extent that we're confident in the end markets and confident in the cycle, we'd be looking to spend over and above that capital guidance that we put out last year.
Mig Dobre
Senior Research Analyst and Associate Director of Research, Baird
Very helpful. Thank you, guys.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
Thanks, Mig.
Operator
Our next question comes from Don Wiley from Northcoast. Please go ahead with your question.
John Healy
Managing Director and Research Analyst, Northcoast
Thanks. Just two quick questions for me. Was just hoping to understand on the acquisition side of things. How do we think about the revenue contribution for acquisitions for the year? I know you said it was about 25% of the growth in Q1. Is that a good proxy to use for the rest of the year? Or is the contribution from those lines different? Just a clarification question. The 4% rate this quarter, and then your kind of, you know, optimism that it could potentially get better from here. Is that what's baked into the guidance? Is +4% price, you know, is that the number that's in the guide, or is there a different number there?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
You undercover Don Wiley from Northcoast? Sounds like.
Elizabeth Higashi
VP of Investor Relations and Sustainability, Herc Holdings
John, do you
John Healy
Managing Director and Research Analyst, Northcoast
Yeah. I am undercover. Yeah.
Elizabeth Higashi
VP of Investor Relations and Sustainability, Herc Holdings
Sorry, John.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
You're on a pseudonym?
Elizabeth Higashi
VP of Investor Relations and Sustainability, Herc Holdings
We were wondering if you, John, are you?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
John, I think so, acquisitions, if you think it through, you know, almost 500 we did last year. The full impact of that is running into Q1 under the guidance as expected, right? That's not part of the raise. We did the larger acquisition, Cloverdale, which we just closed yesterday. That has the most impact on the lift and guidance, and that's factored into the raise. Then what was the other part of your question?
John Healy
Managing Director and Research Analyst, Northcoast
Pricing.
Elizabeth Higashi
VP of Investor Relations and Sustainability, Herc Holdings
Price.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
Pricing. Yeah. We've got 4.3% rate in Q1. We're saying we're gonna grow that every quarter this year. We do have more than 4.3% pricing factored into our guidance.
John Healy
Managing Director and Research Analyst, Northcoast
Okay. Then just on the M&A side of things. How would you characterize you know the pipeline there? Obviously, you guys are talking about wanting to get more fleet. Should we interpret that same level of optimism and you know enthusiasm to be on the M&A side? You know, you know, maybe there's, you know, more properties like you closed in the quarter on the horizon for the rest of the year, or are you gonna take some time and kinda try to level things out a bit?
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings
No, we have a fairly robust pipeline of, you know, both smaller and larger acquisitions that are strategically located in markets and in product lines that focus on what we wanna do in our Top 50 MSAs. It's a robust funnel, and we hope to continue along the same path that we demonstrated in Q1 and early Q2.
John Healy
Managing Director and Research Analyst, Northcoast
Great. Look forward to it. Thanks, guys.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
Thanks, John.
Elizabeth Higashi
VP of Investor Relations and Sustainability, Herc Holdings
I think we have time for one more question.
Operator
Our final question today comes from Steven Fisher from UBS. Please go ahead with your question.
Steven Fisher
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Great. Thanks for taking the questions. I think you mentioned to Ross earlier that you don't expect any change in the inflation to your fleet purchases. Just curious, is that because there are no further surcharge requests or increases in that pricing this year from your major suppliers after sort of the agreements last year? Or is it you're just able to say, "Hey, you know, no, thanks. We already have our agreements for this year?
Larry Silber
President and CEO, Herc Holdings
Well, we have had, you know, some, very few, less than a handful of requests from some suppliers for, you know, some consideration around surcharges based on incremental costs. We've been able to, you know, for the most part, avoid that or diminish that. As Mark mentioned earlier, you know, if we did see anything, it would be minimal, and it would happen. You know, we have seven years to recover those costs. The vast majority, you know, I would say 99% of our suppliers have not requested any surcharge. Like I said, less than one handful of suppliers have. It's a very small, you know, factor. Those that have been requested have been, you know, minimal.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
The comment I made was that the cost, the fleet that we received in Q1 was in line with the price. The inflation was in line with what we expected. We do expect cost inflation going forward, so there will be additional cost inflation on that fleet going into 2023 over what we've been paying in Q1 2022.
Steven Fisher
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Okay. That's helpful. You just mentioned the ability to catch up on pricing for fuel costs in Q2 after that big March step up. Is that gonna end up just being sort of a dollar for dollar going forward, where you were less than dollar for dollar offset in, say, February and March? Or, you know, can you actually get that pricing ahead of what the fuel cost increase is and sort of generate a margin on that?
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
We don't charge or we don't recharge. The customers don't use all of our fuel burn, if you like. Only part of that's recovered in the surcharge. With the marginal comeback in Q2, you know, the surcharge went in after the cost increase really late in the quarter, and we'll get the benefit from that going into Q2, which will impact our flow through. No, we don't really, we don't get a dollar for dollar of every unit of fuel that we burn in terms of chargebacks.
Steven Fisher
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Thank you very much.
Mark Irion
SVP and CFO, Herc Holdings
Thank you.
Operator
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time, we've reached the end of today's question and answer session. I'd like to turn the conference call back over to Elizabeth Higashi for any closing remarks.
Elizabeth Higashi
VP of Investor Relations and Sustainability, Herc Holdings
Thank you, Jamie. Thank you all, everyone for joining us on the call today. As always, if you have any further questions, please, don't hesitate to give me a call, and we look forward to seeing you all soon. Thank you.
Operator
Ladies and gentlemen, with that, we'll conclude today's conference call. We do thank you for joining us this morning. You may now disconnect your lines.
